(p-134) Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, also called Fuṣṣilat

Its purpose is to inform that knowledge is only that which the One encompassing everything in power and knowledge has chosen from His knowledge for His servants, so He legislated it for them, and His messengers came to them with it from Him. That knowledge is what drives faith in God and steadfastness in obeying Him, which go together, as was mentioned earlier in az-Zumar in His saying: ﴿Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [az-Zumar: 9]. Its outcome is the complete unveiling, when He, glorified is He, becomes the hearing of the knower by which he hears, "his sight by which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks" — to the end of the sacred hadith, whose meaning is that He grants him success, so that he does nothing but what pleases Him. This is indicated by its name "Fuṣṣilat" through the allusion to [what] is in the verse mentioned in it, this word "from the Book made distinct for a people who know."

The Sajda is by the allusion to what is in its verse of obedience to Him through prostration, which is the nearest means of drawing close to the King, the Judge, and through glorification, which is the first entrance to faith.

* *

"In the name of God," who, due to His encompassing of the attributes of perfection, did not approve of the majesty of the Book except that which is joined with the beauty of action, "the Most Merciful" who encompassed everything with mercy and knowledge, so He made the Book distinct in detail and clarified it to the utmost clarity, "the Most Compassionate" who specified the learned who act with hearing the call and the penetration of the word.

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ [i.e., the wisdom of Muhammad which (p-135) overwhelmed creation].

When Surah Ghafir ended, which stated that the disbelievers argued about the signs of Allah with falsehood, rejoiced in the knowledge of the worldly life that they had, and that when the punishment came they abandoned it, disowned it, and returned to what the messengers had brought, but it was not accepted from them, He knew that any knowledge that does not benefit at the time of severity and punishment is not really knowledge, and that ignorance is better than it. This was difficult for the Prophet (ﷺ), out of fear that the final outcome of his community would be destruction, with persistence in disbelief until the punishment came, and that his predominant condition (ﷺ) would be only warning. Allah, glorified is He, opened this surah by stating that this Qur'an is a mercy for those who have knowledge and a capacity that obliges them to act upon what benefits them. He repeated the description of mercy in the general and the specific sense, indicating that most of the community is under mercy. He also informed that the Book has been detailed in its detail and clarified in its clarification, so that the disputation of the disputant and the plotting of the obstinate and contentious will not harm it, and that it is sufficient in itself, with the inability of creation to produce it, from demanding signs. So He said [informing about a subject (mubtada')]: ﴿A revelation﴾, i.e., gradually sent down, great, ﴿from the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., He who possesses general mercy for the disbeliever and the believer through sending down the Books and dispatching the messengers, ﴿the Most Compassionate﴾ [i.e.] He who particularizes His mercy for the believers by obligating them to what pleases Him from them.

[p. 136] When the listener yearned for an explanation of this revelation, which was sent down piecemeal, [the text] clarified that, despite this, it contains every good. So He said, [as an apposition to "tanzil" (revelation)]: ﴿A Book﴾, meaning: comprehensive, decisive, and dominant.

Since gathering [material] may sometimes lead to confusion, He said: ﴿whose verses have been detailed﴾, meaning: detailed in their essence, ﴿its verses﴾, meaning: they have been made clear with a thorough clarity in both wording and meaning, while being divided into kinds of meanings and into sections and ends that raise the sublime meanings to the highest levels. [He is] ﴿a Qur'an﴾, meaning: comprehensive together with detail. It is also preserved along with its comprehensiveness by what the root of the word "qara'a" (to read/recite) conveys of the sense of holding and keeping. Together with the gathering, the precision, the preservation, and the binding of its wording, it is an unfurled banner whose meanings spread without limit and without end of promise. Rather, [whenever] one scrutinizes it closely, its understanding becomes more magnificent. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿in Arabic﴾, because the tongue of the Arabs is the most spacious of tongues, the deepest in depth, the most abundant in its expanse, the most elevated in its structure, the most eloquent in wording, the clearest in meaning, and the most majestic in its effect upon souls.

Al-Harrali said: It is a Qur'an because of its gathering, a Furqan (criterion) because of its detailing. It was mentioned to alert [the reader] to what is in the natural dispositions and innate constitutions. Its existence is wise, as it informs of the judgments that are required; it is excellent in establishing the balance of justice; it is Arabic because it clarifies everything, as He, exalted is He, said in the surah of the best of narratives [Yusuf]; and it is a detailing of everything, a clarifier that erases disbelief by what it makes evident of the comprehensive scope of God's command; it is preserved because of its comprehensiveness, since it is not specific, and therefore it does not accept deviation from the established ways.

Since it does not become manifest except to one who has the capacity for it, and who constantly clings to the thresholds in humility, and knocks at the doors in submission and love, He said, linking [this] to ﴿detailed﴾ or to ﴿revelation﴾ or to ﴿the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful﴾: ﴿for a people﴾, meaning: people who have strength of perception for what they seek to grasp, ﴿who know﴾, meaning: who have in them the capacity for knowledge and the renewal of understanding, with their soundness of nature, their smooth readiness to submit to the proofs of reason and of revelation, the unity of their minds, the eloquence of their tongues, the soundness of their thoughts, and the depth of their insight. In this there is a rebuke to them, since they do not look at its beauties so that they might be guided by them, as they devote care to examining poems, to the point of judging one over another, and to the extent that they hang some of them upon the honored Ka'ba, as an honor to it. In it there is also an exhortation to them, since they are people of great resolve, to acquire knowledge of it so that they may be free from needing to ask the Jews. In it there is also good news that God will grant the Arabs, after this ignorance, abundant knowledge, and after this disbelief, great and magnificent faith. In the verse there is also an allusion to blaming the ones who make demands, who were referred to at the end of the verse preceding it, since they had already been given what made them independent of it: the verses of this Book, which they were unable to match, contend with, or equal. This is most strange, because it is speech of the same kind as their speech in being Arabic, yet it differs from their speech in that it rises above the peaks of eloquence to a style before which their poetry shrinks and their sermons and rhymed prose fall short. Moreover, it is neither poetry nor rhymed prose at all, nor one of the kinds of their prose, nor one of the types of their sermons. So they were unable to produce anything like it through the passage of ages and the recurrence of eras and centuries. That suffices as a miracle of great strangeness for one who turns to God in repentance.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: Since the surah of Ghafir included an explanation of the condition of the stubborn and of those who deny the signs, and that this is the fruit of their denial and disputing, and since the structure of the surah was built upon this purpose, as evidenced by its opening and its closing, do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieve﴾ [Ghafir 40:4], and His consoling of His Prophet, upon him be the most excellent prayers and peace, with His saying: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ [Ghafir 40:4]? For such [conduct] had already come from others before them, and so He brought upon them the worst outcome and a severe seizing: ﴿The people of Noah and the factions after them denied before them, and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir 40:5]. Their protection is a shield: ﴿Indeed We shall help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir 40:51]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they disputed with falsehood to refute thereby the truth, so I seized them, and how was My punishment﴾ [Ghafir 40:5], meaning: you have seen what befell them, and their report has reached you, so why should these not take heed from them?

﴿Have they not traveled in the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, but God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God﴾ [Ghafir 40:21]. He seized them only for their denial of the signs: ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so God seized them﴾ [Ghafir 40:22]. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned from among the party of the deniers Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun, and He expanded upon the narrative as an alert to the evil outcome of one who is stubborn, disputes with falsehood, and denies the signs. Then He, exalted is He, said after these verses: ﴿Indeed those who dispute concerning the signs of God without any authority that has come to them, there is in their breasts only pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir 40:56], since power and strength are not theirs. ﴿So seek refuge in God﴾ [Ghafir 40:56] from their evil. He created for them something other than themselves, so that they might perceive that the greatest of creations is the one who created them: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir 40:57], and they are not secure from being seized by either of the two creations.

﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or drop upon them pieces from the sky﴾ [Saba' 34:9]. Then He, exalted is He, said after this: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir 40:69]. Indeed their matter is strange in their being turned away from seeking clarification of the signs after their having been made clear. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned their wretched state in the punishment of the Hereafter and their feeble excuse by their saying: ﴿They have gone astray from us; rather, we were not calling upon anything before﴾ [Ghafir 40:74]. Then He, exalted is He, consoled His Prophet (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of God is true﴾ [Ghafir 40:77]. Then He reiterated the warning to them, saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not traveled in the land?﴾ [Ghafir 40:82], to the end of the surah. Nothing of this warning, around which this surah revolves, nor any repetition of the warning against denying the signs, occurred in the surah of al-Zumar. So when I had made clear the purpose of this, [the surah of Fussilat] followed with the mention of the great sign by which God challenged the Arabs, and by which the proof of God, glorified is He, was established over creation. His saying to them was: Beware of what has been sent before you, for Muhammad (ﷺ) has come to you with the clearest sign and the greatest proof: ﴿A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful﴾ [Fussilat 41:2], ﴿a Book whose verses have been detailed, a Qur'an in Arabic for a people who know﴾, ﴿bringing good news and warning﴾ [Fussilat 41:3-4]. This great surah contains, concerning the greatness of the Book, the sublimity of its rank, and the great mercy in it, what is not found in any of its counterparts. Likewise, in eloquence it dazzles the minds at first encounter, so that an eloquent Arab cannot, upon witnessing its proof, pause even briefly, nor does it occur to his mind to contend with any of its verses even briefly. [It is evident] that it is a mighty Book: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat 41:42]. ﴿Had We made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: Why are its verses not detailed?﴾ [Fussilat 41:44], "non-Arabic and Arabic?" Thus He, glorified and exalted, rebuked them, refuted their argument, humbled their falsehood, and silenced their claims. Then He said: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; and those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness to them; those are called from a far place﴾ [Fussilat 41:44]. ﴿Only those who hear respond﴾ [An'am 6:36]. He also rebuked them for the feeble answer they gave to His clear proof, by their saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings against what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾ [Fussilat 41:5], and their saying: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it﴾ [Fussilat 41:26]. This is a testimony from them against themselves of their incapacity to oppose it, and an acknowledgment of the strength of its challenge. Then He exposed them with His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from God and you have disbelieved in it?﴾ [Fussilat 41:52], and so on. The surah also bears, along with this, the explanation of the destruction of those who were stubborn and denied among those who came before them, who were greater in strength than they. These are the ones He had mentioned in summary in the surah of Ghafir, in the two verses ﴿Have they not traveled in the land?﴾ [Ghafir 40:21] and [﴿Have they not traveled?﴾ [Ghafir 40:82]]. So He, exalted is He, spoke in detail, elaborating on part of that summary: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat 41:13]. Then He said: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said: Who is stronger than us in power?﴾ [Fussilat 41:15]. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾ [Fussilat 41:16], the verse, then He said: ﴿As for Thamud﴾ [Fussilat 41:17]. Thus He made clear [, exalted is He,] their state and seized them. Thus the joining of the two surahs and the connection of the two aims are strengthened, and God knows best. [End.]

When a person's condition inclines toward fear, which is panic (al-halaʿ), or toward hope, which is exultation (al-baṭar), and nothing sets him right except moderation (al-iʿtidal), the balance that leads to perfection, which for his nature is like preserving health and warding off sickness for his body, He said, describing "a Qur'an" as ﴿bashīran﴾, that is, a bringer of good news for whoever follows it, ﴿wa-nadhīran﴾, that is, a warner for whoever refuses and so is cut off.

Abu Nu'aym narrated in al-Hilya, in the biography of our Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah ennoble his face, said in a sermon of his: "The most wondrous thing in man is his heart, which has sources of wisdom and their opposites. If hope appears to it, greed darkens it; if greed stirs it, covetousness destroys it; if despair takes hold of it, grief kills it; if anger befalls it, rage intensifies; if it is made happy by contentment, it forgets caution; if fear seizes it, sorrow preoccupies it; if calamity strikes it, anxiety breaks it; if it gains wealth, riches make it rebellious; if need grips it, affliction preoccupies it; if hunger exhausts it, weakness keeps it seated. So every shortfall in it is harmful, and every excess in it is corrupting."(p-142)

Since their custom was to be constantly cautious with every good-news and warning concerning a worldly matter, He traced their opposition to that custom, in their abandoning resolute certainty (al-hazm [bil-jazm]) by turning away, so He said: ﴿But most of them turned away﴾, that is, from accepting any of its good tidings or warnings, ﴿so they do not hear﴾, that is, they act like one who does not hear. They accept nothing of what it calls them to and urges them upon.

When he had reported their aversion, he reported their estrangement in it, saying: ﴿And they said﴾, meaning, at the time of their aversion, illustrating their remoteness through their refusal to accept: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾, meaning, veils enveloping them. Since the context in Surat al-Kahf concerns majesty, the particle of elevation (*adāt al-istiʿlāʾ*, the particle "upon") was more fitting there, so He said: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. Here they expressed it with the adverbial form (*al-ẓarf*, "in"), to distance them from hearing ﴿of what﴾, meaning, those veils originate from and arise from the matter to which ﴿you call us﴾, O speaker who informs that he is a prophet, ﴿to it﴾. So there is no way for him to reach them, because they completely deny it.

Since the heart is more conscious of what reaches it through the hearing, they said: ﴿And in our ears﴾, which are one of the channels leading to the hearts, ﴿is a deafness﴾, meaning, a heaviness that has made them deaf to hearing it. ﴿And between us and you﴾, meaning, (p-143) originating from the boundary that separates you from us and the boundary that separates us from you, at the midpoint of the distance between them, ﴿is a barrier﴾, a dense screen, so we do not see you to understand you through gesture, and thus the channels of understanding what we say are blocked. ﴿So act﴾, meaning, in accordance with what you hold as your religion. Since repetition of admonition is a place of hope for the admonished's return, they cut off that hope by emphasis through its particle, and they intensified it with the third nūn and the use of the nominal form, so they said: ﴿Indeed, we are acting﴾, meaning, in accordance with what we hold as our religion, so there is no connection between us in any respect, so that none of us would feel shame before the other in his work or turn back to him. Had he said "wa-baynanā" without "min", it would have conveyed that the entire space between them is a barrier, so each of the two parties would be adjacent to its own side, which is half of the void between him and his opponent. In that case, each party would be confined behind its own barrier and unable to act upon us thereafter. Or there would be some connection between them, at least by informing, by whatever means one of the two opposing parties wishes, so the barrier exists. Thus "min" conveys partitiveness (*al-tabʿīḍ*) together with conveying origin (*al-ibtidāʾ*), since they do not affirm a barrier except in matters of religion.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 6:

When they reported their aversion and gave as the reason their failure to understand what he calls them to, Allah, glorified is He, commanded him with a reply that makes clear that they are in pure obstinacy. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these people who are unable to refute any part of your matter with anything that a person of intellect would accept: call upon what cries out against them with their incapacity: ﴿I am only a human being like you﴾, not another kind of being that cannot be seen. A human being sees others of his kind, hears them, and looks at them. So your claim that there is no way for you to reach my sight, or to grasp anything of what I say, has no basis at all.

Since their claim of there being no connection between them had included two things, one concerning themselves and the other concerning what he calls to, and since he had refuted the first, he said regarding the second: ﴿It is revealed to me﴾, that is, by a means that is hidden from you, ﴿that your God﴾, that is, the One who deserves worship, ﴿is one God﴾, not [one of] several. This is something that the sound primordial natures (al-fitar al-ula al-sawiyya, the innate human disposition) have indicated, rational proofs have established, transmitted evidences have confirmed in every age, and on which consensus (ijma') has been concluded in times of spiritual necessity. That is: you are not different from humankind such that your person is hidden from you, like a king, nor is his meaning obscured from them by his speech as with the rest of the animals. And although I am a human being, I am not different from you in kind by being non-Arab; rather I am just like you, equal to you in being Arab. And with all of this, the essence of what has been revealed to me is not expressed in long sentences that become tiresome or are forgotten, or whose understanding is difficult. Rather, it is one single letter, which is tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness). So you have no excuse at all for not understanding it, not hearing it, or not seeing its speaker.

When he cut off their argument and removed their pretext, he made the following a consequence of that, saying: (p-145) ﴿So go straight﴾, that is, seek, aim, and establish uprightness, turning toward Him, even if He is at the farthest distance from you, ﴿to Him﴾, without deviating at all toward any kind of associating partners through an intercessor or anything else.

Since the greatest purpose of revelation is knowledge and action, and since the head of knowledge is tawhid, he identified it and commanded uprightness in it. Then he followed it with the head of action, which is what indicates acknowledgment of incapacity together with striving, so He said: ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾, that is, ask Him for forgiveness of your sins, which is erasing them in essence and in effect, [so that] you are not punished for them, nor reproached by regret over them, and abandoning them both presently and in the outcome.

When He commanded good, He encouraged it and warned against its opposite, so the implied sense of the encouragement is: success and triumph belong to whoever does that. Then He joined to it what the context calls for, saying: ﴿And woe﴾, that is, disgrace and ruin, ﴿to those who associate partners [with Allah]﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 7:

When intellects and revealed laws both bear witness that the essence of felicity lies in two matters: exalting the command of God, and compassion toward the creatures of God, and when the [most excellent] of the gates of exalting the command of God is affirming His oneness (tawhid), then the basest of the deeds between the servant and his Lord is neglecting that, and the basest of the deeds between the servant and the creatures is withholding what God has made obligatory in zakat (alms-tax). The meaning of shirk (association of partners with God) is the judgment that that which has no thing at all belonging to it, and which cannot possibly have any complete ownership over anything at all, has become a partner of Him to whom belongs the whole, in creation and in disposal, regarding what He possesses of complete ownership that (p-146) admits no admixture. And zakat is the association of one who has incomplete ownership with one like himself in a small portion of his wealth.

He said, reproaching those who refused to share with created beings and associated partners with the Creator: ﴿Those who do not give﴾, that is, to their like among the children of Adam, ﴿zakat﴾ from the wealth over which they have no workmanship in its creation, for it is inherited from their father Adam. Analogy requires that they all share in it equally. But We have shown them mercy by assigning to each one of them, by a certain means, what his right hand possesses of it. Yet they have judged regarding the command of their Lord by what they would not accept for themselves, for they refused to share with some of their brethren in some of their wealth, whose ownership of it is weak, by paying zakat, and they associated with Him what owns nothing at all, with what has no benefit alongside the absolute Owner.

Since among what their association and their denial of resurrection entailed was that their miserliness led them to become absorbed in this world and to turn wholly toward its pleasures, they denied the Hereafter. Thus the point of their condition became that they ascribed to one who has no action at all an action that he cannot possibly undertake in any way, and they denied of the Chooser, the Agent, who is responsible for their enormous acts at every time that they witness, and to whom in their benefits and harms they turn, what He affirmed for Himself of His own action. He said, emphasizing, to draw attention to the fact that this denial of theirs is something hardly to be believed: ﴿And they, in the Hereafter﴾, that is, the life that comes after this one and has no after it, ﴿they﴾, that is, specifically among the people of the faiths, ﴿are disbelievers﴾. Thus they stood apart in denying a thing on which no one agreed with them, concerning One whom they witness at every time performing acts more than that. They affirmed for one whom they never witnessed performing any action at all what is not possible for him to do at all, while they claim sound intellects and firm opinions, and they were content for themselves with baseness in withholding [zakat], and they judged God by something even greater than it, while they claim noble character and lofty aspirations. How ugly are such intellects, and how base are such aspirations!

The verse includes that woe belongs to whoever is characterized by three attributes: shirk, which is the opposite of exalting the command of God; refraining from zakat, which is the opposite of compassion toward the creatures of God; and denying the Resurrection, which leads to absorption in what God has hated in the pursuit of this world and its pleasures, and this is of the belittling of the command of God. Al-Asfahani said: The complete statement that there is no addition beyond these three levels is that man has three days: yesterday, today and tomorrow. Knowing what his conditions were yesterday, in eternity, is by knowing the Creator of this world; knowing how the conditions of today should occur is by doing good to the people of knowledge to the extent of one's capacity; and knowing the conditions of the future day is by affirming resurrection and the Last Day. So when a person is opposed to the truth in these three levels, he is in the utmost ignorance and misguidance.

When al-Biqa'i had mentioned what awaits the ignorant (al-jahilin) by way of threat and warning, he then mentioned what awaits their opposites by way of promise and glad tidings. He said, answering one who yearned for this and emphasizing the rejection of one who would deny it:

(p-148) ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾, that is, in what Allah has given them of beneficial knowledge, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, such as zakat and other things, so that their deeds are lawful (shar'iyyan) and beneficial. Since the opening of the surah with "the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" indicated that apparent causes vanish in the presence of the true Cause, which is His mercy, he left the report (al-khabar) without the fa' (the particle of consequence). He said, announcing the greatness of the reward, because its cause is the mercy of the Most Merciful. Had it been with the fa', it would have indicated that it corresponds to the measure of the deed which is its cause: ﴿For them is a reward﴾, that is, a great one, ﴿unending﴾, that is, uncut off, as a recompense for their generosity with the transient, meager wealth in zakat and other things, and for what Allah commanded them of their words and deeds, in the Hereafter and in this world. Al-mamnun means the cut off. From "mannantu al-habl," meaning "I cut the rope by severing its strands." From this is their saying: "The journey has worn him out (qad mannahu al-safar)," meaning it cut him off and removed his strength.

When He (glorified is He) mentioned their foolishness in disbelieving in the Hereafter, He began to mention the proofs of His power over it and over everything He wills in creating the cosmos and what is in it. These proofs encompass them and their objects of worship, including inanimate things and others, and they indicate that He is One, with no partner. So He said, rebuking them [and affirming by the description, because they knew the origin of creation]: ﴿Say﴾ i.e., to the one who denies the Hereafter, rebuking him, by your saying: ﴿Do you indeed﴾ and, to emphasize their denial, He explicitly stated what entails for them of disbelief: ﴿disbelieve﴾ i.e., you truly bring about the reality of covering the apparent lights of the intellects ﴿in the One who created the earth﴾ (p-149) i.e., with its vastness and magnitude, from non-existence ﴿in two days﴾, so you deny His power to restore what He created [from it] at the beginning, while you acknowledge that He began its creation and the creation of that from it. These two days are Sunday and Monday. This is reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Abdullah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn al-Jawzi said: and most scholars. The hadith (prophetic report) of Muslim that preceded in Surat al-Baqarah, "Allah created the clay on Saturday," contradicts this, for the beginning in it is with Saturday, and it explicitly states that the creation of the earth and what is in it was in six days, as is the apparent meaning of this verse. It is answered that the meaning of creation in that hadith is bringing forth its sustenance in actuality, while the meaning here is preparing it to accept that. It is also objected that days occur only through the rotation of the spheres, and that this happened only after the completion of creation in actuality. So the apparent meaning of "day" is what al-Harrali said: the measure in which a manifest matter is completed, or the measure of two days that you know from the days of this world.

When He mentioned their disbelief in resurrection and other things, He conjoined to "you disbelieve" His saying: ﴿and you make﴾ i.e., along with this disbelief ﴿for Him rivals﴾ from among what He created, so you attribute to Him actions and sayings, although you have not seen any of that. Thus you deny what you do the like of, and greater than it, and affirm what you have never done at all. This is the manifest error.

When He rebuked them for their vile belief, its gravity was magnified by magnifying His glorified majesty, so He said: ﴿That﴾ i.e., the great God ﴿is the Lord of the worlds﴾ i.e., their Originator and Sustainer. That definitively indicates [all] the attributes of perfection that He has.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 41, verse 10:

When He had mentioned what they acknowledge of its origination (*ibda'*), He followed it with what He placed in it of wonders. He said, conjoining it to what its sense implies, meaning that He originated the earth as mentioned: ﴿And He placed﴾. It is not permissible to conjoin it to the complement of the relative pronoun (*silat al-mawsul*, the clause that completes the relative), because of the intervening foreign element. ﴿in it firm mountains﴾ [it is the strongest of them], and they are the mountains. He drew attention to the fact that they differ from the *rawasi* (firm things) in being beneath what is to be anchored, so He said: ﴿above it﴾, and they prevent it from shaking. He did this because it is more indicative of power. For if they were beneath it, one would suppose they were carrying pillars. Also, so that the benefits of the mountains would appear in themselves and in what is in them, and so that one would observe that they are weights in need of a bearer. When He had prepared it for what is intended from it, He mentioned what He deposited in it, and said: ﴿and He blessed in it﴾, that is, He made it receptive, facilitated, and fit for sustenance and benefits, from essences and meanings that aid the excellences of the labourers, facilitated for travelling towards Him and turning to Him. It also points to all His beautiful attributes, His exalted names, and other knowledge, measures, and powers. ﴿and He ordained in it its sustenance﴾, that is, He made it, together with the blessing, according to a measure it does not exceed, and according to a wondrous method which He arranged in eternity and approved, and which He decreed and executed. Among that is that He specified some lands with something not found in others, in order to organize the cultivation of the whole earth through people's need of one another. Thus all that preceded, of its deposit and origination, was the mention of its provisions in a single stage, which does not fall short of the needs of the needy at all. Rather, what falls short is their access to it, or the access of some of them to it, so that one then finds nothing sufficient for himself, while the earth contains many times his sufficiency. Then He mentioned the summary of the creation of the earth and what is in it, and said: ﴿in four days﴾. This number, when the two previous days are added to the two days of the sustenances, which are Tuesday and Wednesday, or the meaning in its completion is four days. It is not taken literally as six, because two days for the heavens will come later, so that they would be eight, which would contradict the verse of Alif Lam Mim al-Sajdah: ﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾ [al-Sajdah: 4]. He specified the amount of time in which He created it and the amount He assigned to the sustenances and benefits, because of the comprehensiveness of knowledge that each of the two matters is specified with two days. He stated the first two explicitly, so that this would be more indicative of power. Thus the rebuke against them is well placed, through what He distinguished in the two verses regarding taking rivals. It was more indicative of power because it is the bringing into existence of perceptible essences from non-existence, self-subsisting, unlike blessing and the determination of sustenance, which is a matter that does not subsist by itself. Therefore He did not single out the two days with mention, but made them secondary, just as what was determined in them is secondary. He did not do this in less than the blink of an eye, despite His complete power over it, because this is more indicative of choice and more inclusive of testing and choosing, so that He may lead many astray thereby and guide many thereby. Thus it is greater in their rewards, because it is more indicative of their submission. He made the duration of its creation double the duration of the heaven, although it is smaller than the heaven, as an indication that it is the one intended in itself, because of the two weighty ones (*al-thaqalan*, humans and jinn) in it. It surpasses by what is in it of abundance of benefits and diversity of kinds of accidents and substances, because that is more inclusive of favour upon its inhabitants and of care for their affairs and its affairs. It also surpasses by what is in it of trial through preparation for disobedience, struggles, and remedies, in which the Exalted Assembly compete and dispute. All of this indicates that the duration is not for the sake of power, but for drawing attention to what is in what is determined of what is decreed and to the wonders of affairs. And so that one may also know, by the creation of the heaven, which is greater in body, firmer in substance, greater in adornment, and more abundant in benefits beyond comparison, in less than the duration of the creation of the earth, that its creation in that duration is not out of inability to bring it into being in less than a blink, but for wisdoms that minds cannot bear. Perhaps the specification of the heaven with the shorter duration, rather than the reverse, is to regulate its matter according to what we know, that building a roof is lighter than building a house, as a reminder that He built the affair of this our abode upon causes, teaching patience and training in tranquility and distance from haste.

Since the word ﴿sawā'an﴾ (equally, evenly), which means justice that neither exceeds nor falls short of the half, requires two parties, as you say: "Zayd and 'Amr are equal," and "to a word that is equal between us and you," the Exalted said, removing what the phrase ﴿four days﴾ might have implied, namely that it is for the sustenances and blessing, so that with the two days of the earth it would be six, placing ﴿sawā'an﴾ in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: the distribution is into two days and two days in equality, ﴿for the seekers﴾, that is, for whoever asks, or whoever is such that he asks and his inquiry intensifies, through a question or reflection, about reconciling the apparent meaning of this verse with other verses. This cannot be achieved except between two days and two days, not between two days and four, where neither of the two portions exceeds the other two days by an atom, with comprehensive knowledge and all-encompassing power. This is not like the days of this world, in which each day must be more or less than the one before it. The total of the four is like four days of this world, neither exceeding nor falling short of them. The reading of Ya'qub with the genitive ﴿sawā'in﴾ makes it an adjective of ﴿arba'a﴾ (four). The reading of Abu Ja'far with the nominative is the predicate of an omitted subject. Regarding its creation and completion in four days, its seasons were four. Ibn Burjan said: Do you not see that the command descends to the heaven first, in the sending down of water, and He creates it there, then sends it down to the earth; and the plants and animals, from the water that descends from the heaven to the earth, are like the offspring between male and female, and like the subjection of the heaven and the earth and what is between them for that for which they were made. So understand. It is an upright matter and a widespread wisdom: the sign of His decree is the blessings of the earth in four days, through what He ordained in the heaven of affairs, which are the four seasons of the year: winter, spring, summer, and autumn. These days are known by observation, and in them the earth's cultivation is completed, along with the blessings of the world and all that it brings forth of benefits and wonders. He said: His saying ﴿for the seekers﴾ is an expression of wonder, strangeness, and magnification of the meaning intended by the address. The meaning of ﴿sawā'an﴾ may also extend to what preceded: that by these four days the year's risings and settings, its nearness and distance, its heights and descents, in the northern and southern parts of its zodiacal signs, were equalized, with all of that and its consequences perfected. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 11:

When the heavens were greater than the earth in their essence, by the light of their structures, their expanse, their adornment, the revolution of their spheres, and their height, he drew attention to this by using the particle of sequence (thumma), the word "istiwa'" (rising/turning to), and the particle of limit (hatta-type "ila" of ultimate aim), which indicates the great care taken. So He said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, that is, He intended an intention whose intended end is the intention itself, ﴿to the heaven, while it﴾, that is, and the state of it being, ﴿was smoke﴾, after He had split it from the earth. They said: that smoke was the vapor of water, so it is a borrowing from what rises from fire, and it is a figurative comparison. Thus the heaven precedes the earth in being smoke, as the male precedes the female. Then the earth's own substance was created, and after the shaping and completion of the heaven, the earth was spread out and made into a female, and it was made even, to match the mention of the heaven. Ibn Burjan said: whoever believes that the heaven came first in existence and completion, and the earth after it in existence and rank, and that the days of creation were two days for the creation of the earth, two days for the arrangement of the heaven after it had been smoke, and two days for the completion of benefits, then the numbers overlapped because the actions overlapped. ﴿So He said to it﴾, that is, immediately after this turning, ﴿and to the earth﴾, after its creation and before its spreading out: ﴿Come, both of you﴾, that is, come and approach, both willing and compliant with what I have decreed in you and intended from you, namely the bringing forth of benefits from waters, plants, minerals and other things, in conformity with what I have decreed in you and intended from you of bringing forth benefits from waters, plants, minerals and others. He placed the verbal noun in the position of the circumstantial state for emphasis, so He said: ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾, that is, obedient or reluctant in bringing forth what I have deposited in you of trust, at its appointed times and in accordance with its proper measures and forms, obedience of subjection, not of obligation. (p-156) ﴿They said: We come﴾, that is, we and what is in us, in what is between us.

When He made them the object of address, which is for rational beings, and speech, He spoke including both of them, in regard to their individuals and what is in them, with the plural of those who understand: ﴿obedient﴾, that is, in everything You have inscribed in us, we bear none of that as a burden, but we yield it in accordance with what You commanded, without altering or changing. That is their yielding of the trust and their not bearing it. The plural of the command addressed to them in the report does not indicate plurality in time; rather the speech to them may have been successive.

﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ﴾ means: He created them and fashioned them, while they were ﴿seven heavens﴾ in number, fashioned with a penetrating making that is like a decree, admitting no contradiction ﴿in two days﴾. That is, Thursday and Friday, when the calculation is made of the portion of creation that belongs to them within the six days in which all of the two horizons (al-Khafiqayn) and what lies between them came into being. That portion was equal to what was allotted to a single earth and its sustenance, neither exceeding nor falling short of the period of either of the two days, so that what He allotted to the two days was a third of the total. Ibn Jarir said: The day of Friday (yawm al-Jumu'ah) was so named because Allah, exalted is He, gathered (jama'a) in it the creation of the heavens and the earth. That is, He finished that and completed it.

﴿وأوْحى﴾ means: He cast by a hidden way and by a firm, decisive command ﴿in every heaven its command﴾ (q-157). That is, the command by which He arranged them and arranged their benefits, in a firm order that does not fail, and a binding rein that does not loosen.

When He had spoken in general terms, He singled out what belongs to the nearest heaven, as an indication of honouring us. He turned the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, alerting to the magnitude of this verse, saying: ﴿And We adorned﴾, that is, by what We have of majesty, ﴿the nearest heaven﴾, that is, the one nearest to you, for your sake, ﴿with lamps﴾ of shining stars and their brightness shining forth from them. This does not conflict with their being in other things that are higher than them. The context indicates that what is meant is "an adornment" and "We guarded it with them, a guarding" against the devils.

So the verse is of the ihtibak (interlocking device, the Arabic rhetorical figure of omitting from each of two parallel elements what is indicated by the other): the verb of guarding is omitted, indicated by the verbal noun, and the verbal noun of adornment is omitted, indicated by the verb derived from it.

Since this was a striking matter, He alerted to its greatness by His saying, turning the address to the two attributes of might and knowledge, to inform that these two are the foundation of greatness and its pivot: ﴿That﴾, that is, this lofty command and wondrous affair, ﴿is the decree of the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome by anything while He overcomes everything, ﴿the Knowing﴾, who encompasses all things in knowledge. And just as He, glorified is He, decreed that by His might and knowledge, He decreed that the enduring might would only be conferred by what He legislated of knowledge. In closing with these two attributes there is good news for the community that was addressed with them: that He will grant it of His might and knowledge, especially through gifts and what resembles them of natures and other things, what He has not granted any nation before it. [The secret of His, glorified is He, creating what is knowing within a period, and not in an instant, and making it six, neither fewer nor more, is that if He had created it in an instant, that would have been a doubt for whoever says that He is an agent by essence and not by choice. So the situation required a number. Then the situation required that it be six, because it is the first number that indicates perfection, for it is a complete number, its parts (its fractions) neither exceed it nor fall short of it. That indicates that the agent possesses the qualities of perfection and the attributes of completeness and exaltedness. He did not create it in any number below that, because it is deficient. He created the earth in two days, because two is a number that indicates oneness, so it leads the servants to monotheism. He made the two days repeated with respect to their essence and their benefits, as a warning of the disobedience that occurs in them through association (shirk), which is duality and falsehood. He did not repeat it for the heaven, because its signs are more indicative of monotheism, and there did not arise from its people what indicates threat. And so that its creation in less than the duration of the earth, though it is greater in body, more wondrous in making, and more perfect in form, would be more indicative of action by choice, with wondrous wisdoms and extraordinary great secrets.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 13:

When this degree of knowledge was necessitating submission to every good, including tawhid (divine oneness) and other matters, and turning toward the truth in every affair, the one who persists in his aversion even after admonition [with it] is as though he has renewed an aversion other than his first aversion. He said, detailing part of his statement, ﴿But if most of them turn away﴾ [Fussilat: 4], ﴿if they turn away﴾, i.e., they persist in their aversion, or others turn away from accepting the reminder that you have brought them (p-159) after this clear exposition in these verses, which indicated, with the most complete indication, oneness, knowledge, power and other attributes of perfection. ﴿Then say﴾, i.e., to them: Indeed, you have predecessors whose path of obstinacy you have taken. If you refuse except to persist, we will join you with them as their like. This is the meaning of ﴿I have warned you of a thunderbolt﴾, i.e., the descent of a thunderbolt prepared for one to whom the matter has been made plain and who then persists in obstinacy, for the duty of proof has been completed in the most perfect manner. Al-Baghawi and Ibn al-Jawzi said: "The thunderbolt is that which destroys everything" – end of quotation. The summary is that it is a punishment of severe impact, as though in the severity of its impact it is a thunderbolt.

When warning with something whose like is easy to witness is more effective upon the soul, he said: ﴿like the thunderbolt of ʿAd and Thamud﴾, i.e., those whose dwellings you see and whose remains you regard with awe. He explained the descent of that [upon them] with his saying:

**﴿إذْ﴾** It is also possible that it is an adverb of time governing *ṣāʿiqah* (the thunderbolt). Its being a temporal adverb does not contradict its being a causal particle, meaning: **﴿when the messengers came to them﴾**, because a long period of time permits attributing to it what happened in one part of it. Since the messengers only came with the act in part of the time, he introduced the preposition, saying: **﴿from before them﴾**, meaning: from their front, because the first warner is a warner to everyone who came after him, that if he commits what they committed, what they were punished with will come to him. **﴿And from behind them﴾**, meaning: those who came to them, because they (p-160) did not know of their coming. So "behind" is a metaphor for concealment, and "in front" a metaphor for clarity. There is no doubt that when a person is obeyed by someone from his front, and that person hears from him, he turns to what he sees with his own eye, because the soul does not submit to what opposes it except after dispute and struggle. When time lengthens and others submit to him, the matter becomes easy for it and its burden is lightened. Also, the one who comes to people comes to them after their existence and their reaching the threshold of responsibility, so he comes to them from behind them, meaning after their existence. Or "what is before them" is the one who came to them, because they knew of his coming as one who looks from in front of him, and "what is behind them" is what was hidden from them of those who preceded them, so their reports were transmitted to them only in forms that admit criticism. Or the meaning is: their messenger came to them, who, by manifesting the miracle, like all the messengers, by admonition from every side, which is hidden from them or becomes clear to them, and he employed every stratagem and every proof with them, until he left them no doubt. Then he explained that the coming of the messengers negates the worship of other than God and restricted worship to Him, so he said, manifesting with the worship the name that is more deserving of it: **"that"**, meaning: that they said to them: **﴿Worship none but God﴾**, meaning: the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection.

(p-161) Since this was a place where the listener eagerly awaits their report at that point, the answer was given by their saying: **﴿They said﴾**, meaning: each of them: **﴿Had our Lord willed﴾**, meaning: the One who nurtured us in the best upbringing and made us among His elect by the blessings He bestowed upon us, that He should send a messenger to us, **﴿He would have sent down angels﴾**, meaning: to us, **﴿so He would have sent them to us with what He desires from us. But He did not send down angels, so He did not will to send a messenger.** Thus, from what they said there arises an exceptive syllogism (*qiyās istithnāʾī*), in which they inferred the negation of its consequent, the negation of its antecedent, because they assumed between the antecedent and the consequent a necessary connection (*mulāzamah*) according to their claim. Their saying is: **﴿Indeed we, in what﴾**, meaning: because of which. Since they did not deny the messengership in its absolute sense, but only denied that it was from God, they constructed their statement in the passive voice, the Exalted giving precedence in the rendering of their speech to the second person over the third person, because that is more effective in showing the scarcity of their courtesy: **﴿you have been sent﴾**, [meaning]: O messengers, and whoever is in the same condition as them of mankind, **﴿with it﴾**, meaning: [in] what you claim exclusively, not with anything other than what you have been sent with, such as that which angels were sent down with, for example, **﴿we disbelieve﴾**, because our syllogism has indicated that He, the Exalted, did not will the sending, so you are not sent from Him, because you are human and not angels. They lied in their syllogism, which they did not take from reason or transmission, because there is no necessary connection between the will to send to people in general or to a community among them, and that the ones to whom he is sent are all angels.

(p-162) When He had gathered them together in what they had gathered upon, to the point that it was as though they had mutually agreed upon it, He detailed what they had differed over, saying, giving the cause of what preceded of their speech: ﴿As for ʿĀd﴾, that is, the people of Hūd, peace be upon him, ﴿they were arrogant﴾, that is, they sought arrogance and brought it into being ﴿in the earth﴾, that is, all of it, the part in which they were actually present and the remainder of it potentially; or, in its entirety actually, because they possessed all of it. Since arrogance may be in accordance with truth, as it is for one who opposes the command of God, He said: ﴿without right﴾, that is, without a matter that corresponds to reality, namely denying the messengership of human beings, since the reality is that they are sent. ﴿And they said﴾, that is, they added to their arrogance toward accepting what had come to them of the truth that they said, exalting themselves against the command of God, with what God had bestowed upon them of His bounty: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ For we are able to repel the punishment that will come, with which Hūd, peace be upon him, threatens us, because they were the strongest of people in power and the greatest of them in bodies.

Since the expected wording would be, as a rebuke to them: "Have they not seen that God, if He willed, would have made them like others," He followed it with His saying: ﴿Did they not see﴾, that is, did they not know with a knowledge that is like direct witnessing, because it is an innate disposition in the original nature, so it is necessary knowledge ﴿that God﴾, that is, the One encompassing everything in power and knowledge, ﴿who created them﴾ when they were nothing, ﴿is mightier than them in strength﴾. Whoever knows that another is stronger than himself and is sensible submits to Him in what benefits him and does not harm him. The combination of their strength, which is firmness of constitution, and His strength, glorified is He, which is perfection of power and is an attribute subsisting in His essence, glorified is He, is only in the effects arising from strength; therefore they were joined with the superlative form ("mightier").

Since He clarified that they had brought arrogance into being, He followed it with what is the root of every evil among their dispositions, saying [clarifying the extent of their ignorance through their audacity toward the greatness whose matter is to break the oppressor and seize the sinner]: ﴿And they were﴾, that is, by nature for them, ﴿toward Our signs﴾, in light of the greatness they possess by their being attributed to Us.

﴿Denying﴾, that is, rejecting with a denial before which every denial is dissolved, in obstinacy, while knowing that they are from Us.

﴿So We sent﴾ against them, because of that, in keeping with the greatness that belongs to Us, and by the particle of elevation He indicated their insignificance and lowliness when He said: ﴿against them﴾. He increased their humiliation by informing that He destroyed them for the sake of what they took pride in, namely the strength of their bodies and the sturdiness of their frames, by means of what is the most subtle of things in body, which is air, so He said: ﴿a wind﴾, that is, a great one, ﴿exceedingly cold﴾, that is, intensely cold, loud and violently blowing, to the point that it froze the body with its cold, so that it was as if it ﴿constricted﴾ it (that is, gathered it) into one place, preventing it from acting with its strength, and it cut the heart with its sound, overwhelming its courage, and with the severity of its cold it burned everything it passed over.

Since in this context their arrogance in the aforementioned manner had been mentioned, and their claim that they were the strongest of people, the situation required their humiliation in their destruction. So He mentioned "days" without "nights," although the nights are included, and He said, may He be exalted: ﴿on days﴾. [Since] the plural of paucity (jam' al-qilla) [may] be used figuratively for abundance, He confirmed that the intended meaning is paucity by describing them with the sound plural (jam' al-salama), so He said: ﴿ill-omened﴾. This was more indicative of this intended meaning than the singular "day," as in the case of "the moon," because the singular may refer to a period in which a clear matter is accomplished even if its duration is long, while the plural may be used for the genus, which includes with the few whatever is suitable for the plural of abundance. In it, together with its being a warning, there is an allusion to the one upon whom this revelation was sent down, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the greatest good news, in keeping with what the opening of the surah with the name of Mercy alluded to, and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿for a people who know﴾ [Fussilat: 3], that for his people there will be strength and knowledge. And whoever joined warning with good news in His saying: ﴿a bearer of good news and a warner﴾ [Fussilat: 4], and whoever made the days of this punishment eight, pointed to forbearance and deliberation, just as the preceding creation of this existence in six days indicated it, although He was able to both punish and create in a single instant. Thus this indicated that in the sixth year of the Hijra there would be the causal conquest through the lesser pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiyya, which was the occasion of the revelation of Surat al-Fath; and in the seventh year there would be the 'umra which was harder for them than the striking of the sharp, cutting sword, to the extent that 'Amr ibn al-'As went to Habasha (Abyssinia) because of it, so that he would not see what he could not bear of the entry of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, [p-165] into it; and in the eighth year there would be the true conquest with ten thousand fighters, most of them armored, of whom nothing could be seen but the pupils of the eyes, so that they took the whiteness of their mothers for mirage, and thus they thought the utmost punishment was coming upon them, but they were a mercy. As for 'Ad, they saw the cloud and thought it was mercy, but it was a punishment and a vengeance. Describing it with ill-omen is an intensive form, like "a just man," to indicate that it was capable of affecting the body and the powers that were in it by this wind. It is a verbal noun pluralized because of the differing kinds of ill-omen in it. This is according to the reading of the majority with a sukun on the ha' (ﻧَحْسات / nahsat), but the reading of Ibn 'Amir and the Kufans with a kasra on the ha' (نَحِسات / naḥisat) is an adjective from a verb with kasra, like "fariḥa, fa-huwa fariḥ." The first of these days was Wednesday according to the view of Yahya ibn Salam, and another said: no people was punished except on a Wednesday. ﴿So that We may make them taste﴾ and he added the qualified noun to its qualifier for emphasis, from the pattern of "a man of justice," so He said: ﴿the punishment of disgrace﴾, that is, which will humiliate them, expose them and abase them, because they magnified themselves and boasted against the word of Allah which His messengers brought to them. He described the punishment with disgrace, which belongs to the one punished by it, as an intensive form, to emphasize its disgracing of him. ﴿In the life of this world﴾, so that they would be humiliated before those whom they had magnified over themselves in the abode by which they were deceived and so became arrogant in it, for that is more indicative of power to one bound by illusion. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter﴾, which is prepared for the arrogant, ﴿is more disgracing﴾, that is, more intensely humiliating, as they say: "he gave him the dirhams and gave him preference for kindness." He emphasized it because of their denial of it.

Since their defense of themselves was negated, He negated the defense of others, so He said: ﴿and they﴾, that is, this punishment befell them and the punishment of the Hereafter will befall them, while they are ﴿not helped﴾, that is, no help will be found or renewed for them ever, in any way whatsoever.

When he finished mentioning the thunderbolt of the people [of Lot and 'Ad], he began to explain the thunderbolt of Thamud, saying: ﴿As for Thamud﴾, and they were the people of Salih, peace be upon him. ﴿We guided them﴾, [i.e.] we made clear to them the path of guidance, that We are capable of resurrection and of everything, and that We have no partner. This was made clear to them by the she-camel in the fullest clarity. They saw that with their eyes, which are the cause of the seeing of their insight to the fullest extent. But they disliked that, because of what it entails, namely deviating from the path of their forefathers, and they turned to holding fast to the path of their forefathers. ﴿But they preferred blindness﴾, i.e. the misguidance resulting from blindness of sight or of insight, or both together, ﴿over guidance﴾, i.e. they produced, through deeds and words, what indicates their love of that and their pursuit of loving it. So they became blind and went astray. Al-Qushayri said: It was said that they had believed and affirmed, then apostatized and denied, so He treated them in the same way as their brethren regarding annihilation.

﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾, i.e. because of that, a seizing of compulsion and disgrace. And He intensified its description by making it the very humiliation itself, so He said: ﴿the humiliating﴾, i.e. the one possessing humiliation. Its damma (the vowel u on the first letter of "al-Huni") took the place of what is in the word "al-hawan" (humiliation) of the form (of the adjective), so it is known that the meaning is that He is the one who humiliates and disgraces. ﴿For what they used to earn﴾, i.e. continually, ﴿earning﴾, i.e. their acquiring it continuously and counting it is beneficial. So the verse is of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are mentioned and each is omitted from the other side): He mentioned guidance first as an indication of the omission of misguidance second, and blindness second as an indication of the omission of seeing first. Its secret is that He attributed to Himself the nobler of the two verbs, and ascribed to them what no living being would be pleased with [dhu al-ruh].

Now that he had finished the report about the disbelievers of both groups, he followed it with a report about their believers, as good news for those who followed the Prophet (ﷺ) and as a warning for those who turned away from him. So he said: ﴿And We saved﴾ [i.e.]: a great deliverance ﴿those who believed﴾, i.e., they brought this attribute into being, even at its least degree, from both groups ﴿and were﴾, i.e., with a great state of being ﴿mindful of God﴾, i.e., this attribute renews itself for them in every movement and stillness, so they do not proceed to anything without evidence.

(p-168) When he had mentioned their condition in this world and alluded to the condition of the Hereafter, he followed it with a detailed account of that, saying: ﴿And [mention] the day﴾, i.e., remember the days of the enemies of Allah in this world, when His punishment descended upon them and His exemplary chastisements settled in their courtyards; and remember the day when they are gathered. This was the original wording, but he specified what they were punished with, so that it would encompass everyone who was characterized by it among the earlier and later generations, and said: ﴿they are gathered﴾, i.e., they are assembled in great numbers by a compelling command, without any burden on Us in it. This is according to the reading of the majority (al-Jama'ah), with the verb in the passive voice; and according to the reading of Nafi' and Ya'qub with the nun, in the active voice, it is in view of the context of ﴿and We saved﴾. In both readings there is the sense of majesty, and therefore the Greatest Name is appropriate to both, being greater than the manifestation of majesty from which the turning away occurred, because mentioning it carries greater reproach for them, abhorrence of their deed, and debasement of their intellects, in His saying: ﴿the enemies of Allah﴾, i.e., of the Greatest King. Its i'rab (grammatical analysis) according to each reading is not hidden. ﴿To the Fire﴾, the abode of the wretched, ﴿so they are held back﴾ because of their being gathered, i.e., they are pushed back and restrained, the first of them being turned back upon the last of them with the least effort; and whoever wishes to deviate from them to the right or to the left, supposing that he may be hidden by reason of their great numbers, is driven back with a driving of humiliation; and whoever of them has strayed is gathered to them. For each of these is a kind of punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 20:

When he had explained their humiliation through being driven back (al-wazʿ), he explained its ultimate ends, saying: ﴿Until, when﴾. He emphasized the statement, because of their denial of its content, by adding the negative particle, so that its combination with the affirmation would be a negation of the opposite, and thus it conveys the utmost strength in the content of the report, in its confirmation, its firmness, and its connection with the testimony at once. So he said: ﴿they come to it﴾, that is, the Fire which they used [to] deny, ﴿their hearing, their sight and their skins will testify against them﴾, at the time of the gathering (al-takwir) in it, piled upon one another. And since it was in the context of warning, and the detail was more dreadful, he said: ﴿their hearing﴾, using the singular because people are close to one another in it, ﴿and their sight﴾, using the plural because of the great difference among them in it, ﴿and their skins﴾, and he affirmed the act (al-kawn) as an explanation, because they were stamped with what made the Fire necessary for them of burdens, so he said: ﴿they used to do﴾, that is, they renewed their deed, persisting in it. It is as if these limbs say at that moment, establishing the conclusive proof: "O created beings, and those present of mankind, the jinn and the angels, know that my companion used to act through me in such and such a way, persisting in it, and therefore deserved the Fire, and the Mighty One became angry." Then he is cast into it.

(p-170) When he had informed them of this [stone-crushing fire], [the verse] informed them that the return to Him did not benefit them, given their coarse disposition and dense dullness. So he said, linking it to what is implied: "This testimony did not benefit them in shame before Allah, nor in humility within themselves, nor in turning away from disputation and obstinacy, just as the mere knowledge of Allah concerning them did not benefit them: ﴿And they will say to their skins, 'Why did you testify against us?'﴾" He included within this what he had explicitly mentioned of their skins' benefit to them, since there was no need for detail. When [the skins] acted as rational beings act, they addressed them as they would address such beings, saying: ﴿Why did you testify against us?﴾

Since this was a matter of wonder for them, and since it implied their ignorance by their supposing that the skins had the power to remain silent, and since their question about the cause was not a genuine inquiry but was meant as reproach, the answer was given, out of eagerness for a reply, with the words, expressing the skins' speech in the form used for rational beings: ﴿They will say [making excuse]: 'Allah has made us speak' [by compulsion], ﴿Allah﴾, who possesses all the attributes of might, in a manner by which we were unable to refrain from it.

Since the state of the disbelievers is always caught between dullness and obstinacy, they gave two witnessing proofs for this, saying: ﴿He who made everything speak﴾, that is, by action, by capacity, or by state and by utterance.

Since all things are equal in their standing before Him, glorified is He, with regard to making speak, making silent, and other such things, of everything that is possible in relation to His power, they alerted them to this by saying: ﴿And He created you the first time﴾. You have certain knowledge that you were non-existent, then drops (nutaf) that do not accept speech in the ordinary course of things in any way, then your state passed through stages of development in the same manner, until He brought you to the realm of perception, and He compelled you (فَقَسَرَكم) to speech such that, if you wished to remove it from yourselves, you would not be able to. Since the creation is one single thing, He expressed it in the past tense. Since the return was sometimes by sense and sometimes by meaning, and since the one by meaning has many repetitions according to the multiplicity of renewal, He said: ﴿And to Him [i.e., to other than Him] you will be returned﴾, that is: at every moment, by His compelling you with the easiest of matters, over everything He wills, from the first moment of your creation to an endless end. So if you had any kind of knowledge, that would suffice you as an admonition in this world, by which you would know that you are in utmost weakness, and that to Him belong greatness, majesty, power, and dominion.

Muslim reported in his Sahih, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said: 'Do you know what I laugh at?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'At the servant's speaking to his Lord. He says: O Lord, did You not protect me from injustice?' He said: 'He says: Yes.' He said: 'Then he says: I will not accept anything except a witness from myself.' He said: 'He says: Sufficient is yourself [today] as a witness, and the noble recording angels as witnesses.' He said: 'Then He seals his mouth, and it is said to his limbs: Speak! So they speak of his deeds. Then he is left alone with speech, and he says: Away with you, and destruction! It was for your sake that I was contending.'"

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 22:

When they made their excuses, their being informed of it in this world was an admonition and a warning, and in the Hereafter it is a rebuke and reproach, they said, repeating the admonition and warning against the whole of existence: (p-172) ﴿And you did not used to conceal yourselves﴾, meaning: with that which is for you like a natural disposition, ﴿conceal yourselves﴾, meaning: you took on the covering of concealment at the time of sins while you were imagining, and this is the meaning of Qatadah in his saying: "you were thinking."

﴿That your hearing would testify against you﴾ regarding those sins. Since the intent is to convey the warning forcefully, he repeated the detail, saying: ﴿your hearing﴾, and he emphasized it by repeating the negation, saying: ﴿nor your sight﴾, he used the plural and singular for what has passed, ﴿nor your skins﴾. Your concealment was only because ﴿you thought﴾, due to your denial of the Resurrection, out of your ignorance, ﴿that Allah﴾, who possesses all perfection, ﴿does not know﴾, meaning: at any moment of time, ﴿much of what you do﴾, meaning: you renew its doing while persisting in it. This is what you used to regard as hidden, and this is what emboldened you to do what you did. If this was your belief, then it is disbelief; otherwise, your action is the action of one who thinks so, and it is close to disbelief. The believer in truth is one who knows that Allah is aware of his secret and his open affairs, so he remains watchful, fearful, and reverent. Al-Shaykhan related in their two Sahihs, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari in the Book of Tawhid, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Two men of Thaqif and a man of Quraysh, or two men of Quraysh and a man of Thaqif, gathered at the House; they had much fat on their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. One of them said: "Do you think that Allah hears what we say?" The other said: "He hears if we speak aloud, and does not hear if we conceal it." Another said: "If He hears when we speak aloud, He hears when we conceal it." So Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not used to conceal yourselves﴾ - the verse. (p-173) Al-Baghawi said: It is said that the Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two in-laws, and the two Qurashis were Rabi'ah and Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 23:

When the mention of disobedience, and what emboldened one to it, implied a deficiency that impugns divinity, he made clear that this was what brings on wrath, and so said: ﴿And that﴾, meaning: the matter, which is monstrous in its ugliness. Then he explained it with his words: ﴿your assumption﴾, meaning: the corrupt one, and he described it with his words: ﴿which you assumed about your Lord﴾, meaning: which [assumed] that He, whose goodness toward you has been long, does not know your condition. Then he informed about it with his words: ﴿has ruined you﴾, meaning: it specifically causes, through it, that He has destroyed you. As for the disobedience of the limbs alongside tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and tanzih (declaring God free of imperfection), its matter is easier. The summary is that every assumption that was not permitted by the Lawgiver (al-Shari') is one that ruins its holder.

When morning was the place where hopes of joys are expected, and the worst of sorrows was that which occurred in it, he said: ﴿so you became﴾, meaning: because what you were given of blessings, so that you might rescue yourselves from destruction, became the cause of your destruction ﴿among the losers﴾, meaning: those utterly drowned in loss, who are judged to have lost throughout that entire day. He portrayed it in the most hideous form, which is morning. The meaning is that when your state becomes the state of one who has arisen in that condition, there is no time left for gain in which to make up for what was lost, unlike if it had occurred in the evening, for then one would await the morning to strive for gain. And the Day of Resurrection has no day after it in which one strives for gain. Therefore, it is fitting for the believer that, when alone in privacy, he be at his utmost in awe of God. (p-174)

Since this was so, the following was its consequence: His saying, turning away from addressing them (idhanan bi-shiddat al-ghadab, "as a declaration of the intensity of anger"), and as an indication that when they reached the state mentioned, speech failed them, so they could not utter a word with the tongue, nor gesture with the head or the fingertip: ﴿Then if they endure, the Fire is their dwelling place.﴾ That is, for what they are being requited with, their endurance benefits them not; and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then the Fire is their abode﴾, that is, a place of lodging for them. ﴿And if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ That is, they will seek contentment by the removal of blame (al-'atab), which is the calling to account for sin. ﴿So they are not among those who are granted satisfaction﴾, that is, those who are pleased, from whom blame is removed [upon them] so that He would pardon them and abandon their punishment.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 25:**

When He mentioned their threat in this world and the Hereafter, He followed it with their disbelief, which is the cause of the threat, and joined it to what its implied sense is: "So We set upon them a disposition of evil that requires they never cease from what calls for reproach. Yet they turned away, and the warnings did not benefit them, [such as] the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud." Then He said, turning the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, to indicate that the control over hearts is a very great matter: ﴿And We appointed﴾, that is: We brought, arranged, sent, caused, entrusted, and prepared, from the root *qayd*, which is the example, and the upper dry shell of the egg, ﴿for them companions﴾, that is: individuals like them in character and attributes (p-175) who were strong. And they, despite being intensely attached to them and encompassing them, being at the utmost degree of misfortune, severity in baseness and wickedness, and obstinacy in that by which the good is constricted and evil is widened, are among the misguided ones of the jinn and mankind. ﴿So they made appealing to them﴾, that is: of the ugly deeds, ﴿what﴾, and it generalized all things, so He did not use a preposition, and said: ﴿before them﴾, that is: they know its ugliness, yet they made it appealing to them, so they committed it and desired it. ﴿And what was behind them﴾ [that is: what they are ignorant of its matter, and they never cease] in every matter they make appealing, insist upon, and repeat until it is accepted, for repetition is indeed influential. Al-Qushayri said: When Allah intends evil for a servant, He appoints for him brothers of evil and companions of evil who urge him toward transgressions and call him to them. When Allah intends good for a servant, He appoints for him companions of good who help him in acts of obedience, urge him toward them, and call him to them. Among these is Satan, and worse than him is the self, and an evil companion it is. It calls today to what brings destruction, and it bears witness tomorrow against it.

Since the sense was: "So they did not call to any ugly deed until they committed it," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And the word was fulfilled﴾, that is: it became due and established ﴿against them﴾, that is: with the perpetuity of anger.

Since this requires intense grief on his part (ﷺ), He lightened it with His saying: ﴿among﴾, that is: being within the group of ﴿nations﴾, that is (p-176) many. Since He described them with what requires their magnification, in that they are intended, He belittled them with the feminine pronoun, saying: ﴿that have passed away﴾, that is: no nation among them took warning from the other. Since passing away may occur through death in their time, He made clear that it is of what has gone by and ended.

Since some of those who passed did not encompass the whole of time, He expressed it with *min* ("from"), saying: ﴿before them﴾, that is: in time. He put the stronger first so that the power over it would be understood as a power over what is less, by way of a fortiori reasoning, for mankind used to consider themselves inferior to the jinn and would seek refuge with them. So He said: ﴿from the jinn and mankind﴾. Then He gave the reason for the rights of wretchedness being due against them, with His saying, alerting by emphasis that they deny that ugly deeds are a cause of loss: ﴿Indeed they﴾, that is: all those mentioned of them and of those before them, ﴿were﴾, that is: by nature and by action, ﴿losers﴾. So the rational person must strive in choosing his companions, intimate friends, and beloved ones, for the outcome with them is either a good and magnificent one or an ugly and grievous one.

Ṣāḥib al-Firdaws narrated from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:
