So he said, expressing with the particle of affirmation (ʾadāt al-taḥqīq) to indicate the predominance of Allah's blessings in this world over His punishments, and to indicate the condition of man upon touching blessing from a direction he expects, after explaining his condition upon touching it suddenly without expectation, as an emphasis on the explanation of his ignorance, since he made the time of blessing a time for turning away without fear of the one who would take it away, given the nearness of his time to hardship: ﴿And when We bestow﴾ from what We have of greatness and kindness ﴿upon man﴾, i.e., the one who stands with himself, a blessing befitting Our greatness, so that good touches him, and he did not express in this side with what he expressed in the one after it, indicating that the one who turns away is a wrongdoer merely by turning away, not by exaggerating in it. So He said: ﴿he turns away﴾, i.e., deviates from the right course of intention toward Us, away from Us, throughout the entire period of the blessing, as the time-expression conveys, so he did not restrict that blessing with gratitude after seeing Our favor, certain that that blessing is pure good outwardly and inwardly, so he seeks its continuation; and it may have been a trial, a gradual leading on (istidrāj) and a test. ﴿And he turns aside﴾, i.e., he moves away with great distancing, such that he places between Us and him a great barrier, while he inclines ﴿by his side﴾, i.e., by his flank, as a metonymy for his arrogance, his self-conceit, his admiration of himself and his pride, and as a depiction of him by one who has been addressed and turns aside and twists away, and goes further astray in his error and deviation.

When the condition of man at touching evil suddenly had preceded, he explained his condition at touching it while expecting it, so he said, expressing regarding the side of evil with the particle of affirmation, contrary to the usual practice of the Qur'an, to indicate that, due to the increase of his ignorance beyond its limit, pride is necessary even if he expects evil, and his state remains that of one who is secure until it mixes with him; then his bonds loosen and he perishes. His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him﴾, i.e., this kind, whether little or much, by Our retribution against him. So the verse is of ihtibak: He mentioned the bestowal first, which indicates the retribution second, and mentioned evil second, which indicates good first. And the teaching of good manners is in attributing the bestowal to Himself and not evil, although all is from Him.

Since the magnification of breadth indicates the greatness of length, he said, expressing with what indicates constancy and permanence: ﴿then he is one of lengthy supplication﴾, i.e., in seeking its removal. It may be that it was an inner blessing and he does not perceive it, and he only supplicates at the moment of touch. He should have begun supplication at the time of expectation, or even before it, seeking acquaintance with Allah the Exalted in ease, so that he would know Him in hardship. This is a noble character trait that only individuals whom Allah has specially favored with His kindness know. So his neglect indicates the lack of his gratitude for what passed, the lightness of his intellect regarding what comes, and his surprise at the necessity of supplication upon touch, indicating the lack of his patience, the thinness of his skin and the scarcity of his modesty. ﴿Broad﴾, i.e., extremely wide in breadth; as for its length, do not ask about it. This is a metonymy for the extreme in abundance.

(p-223) When He, glorified is He, had mentioned some of their conditions, which fall under this whole category and which are evident from observation of existence, namely that they have no steadfastness, especially in times of hardship, in order to inform of their deep-rooted ignorance and incapacity, He indicated both matters together through something no sensible person can deny: they do not countenance what is possible, so they do not prepare for it what would protect them should it occur. He therefore commanded him (ﷺ) to mention this, as a notice of turning away from them and as a sign that their anger had reached its limit: ﴿Say: "Tell me"﴾, that is, inform me, ﴿if it is﴾, that is, this Qur'an, which you have set up to contend against, even to the point of turning away from listening to it by engaging in idle noise during its recitation, such as whistling, clapping, and other things, and this conduct of yours does not proceed from a decisive proof about its matter by which you would be certain with conviction, but rather it proceeds from frivolity and lack of reflection on your part, ﴿from Allah﴾, the One who encompasses all the attributes of majesty and beauty, so He is not contended against.

Since disbelief in it, on this supposition, is extremely remote, and since the purpose of the sura revolves around knowledge, He drew attention to this with the particle of delay (thumma), together with an indication that this disbelief on their part came only after a long reflection. They were thus obstinate, until they descended, with whistling and clapping, from the highest ranks of speech to the voices of dumb animals. So He said (p-224): ﴿then you disbelieve in it﴾, that is, after deep consideration of it and verification, because it is true. By this you are in a schism that is extremely far from harmony with one who never ceases to win you over by his beautiful deeds and to turn you back with his sublime words. ﴿And one other than you believed in it, because it is from Allah.﴾ ﴿Who is more astray﴾ than you, this is what the original structure would have been, but He said instead: ﴿than one who is in extreme schism﴾, that is, against the friends of Allah, ﴿far off﴾, as a warning that they have become so, and that whoever becomes so has exposed himself to the seizures of Allah, the Exalted, by which whoever is struck is destroyed without doubt. And who is more guided than one who is in near submission, namely the one who believed, because he has made peace with Allah, and whoever makes peace with Him, everything makes peace with him, so he is saved from every danger. Thus the verse is of the type called ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which a term is omitted from one clause and left implicit by its counterpart in another): it mentions disbelief first as an indication of belief second, and error second as an indication of guidance first. Its purpose is that mentioning harms is more striking to the heart, and therefore more beneficial in admonition.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 53:**

When this was saddening to the one who is compassionate toward them, because it made clear how far they were from returning, He said, alerting that when Allah, glorified is He, wills that this (return) be very near to them, He turns the speech to the station of Majesty, as a notice that it is easy for Him: ﴿We shall show them﴾, meaning, soon, through a promise that admits no breach, ﴿Our signs﴾, meaning, with the greatness that belongs to them (p. 225) ﴿in the horizons﴾, meaning, the regions. (It is) the plural of ufuq, like unuq and a'naq. The second hamza was changed into an alif because it is sukun after a similar letter. That is, what appears of the regions of the sky or the direction of the winds. This includes what Allah opens of lands through the victory of their people, with each of its battles being one of the markers of prophethood and a great witness sufficient for the soundness of the message, confirming His promise, glorified is He. (It also includes) the destruction of some of their people to aid His prophets and messengers, and what is in them of the wonders of craftsmanship, the strange traces, and the arrangement, with the differences of rulings alongside the agreement of their substances in homogeneity, and other signs that are perceived by sight, which the signs of hearing explain.

Since faith in the unseen is what is considered, and whatever is closer to it is closer to perfection, and the signs of the horizons are closer to that, He began with them. Then He said: ﴿and within themselves﴾, meaning, from the conquest of Makkah, what befell them of the years of famine, the story of Abu Basir and similar matters, and what is distinct for them along with that, what is in the human being himself of marvelous signs, wonders of creation, strange craftsmanship, the marks of origination, the variety of attributes, and other witnesses that correspond to the examples and rational proofs He strikes when considering statements and actions. (It also includes) what is in the lands of the Arabs of visible signs: the denial after their rushing to it and their unanimity upon it, and the affirmation of monotheism among all of them after their distance from it and their fighting against the one who called to it. Glorified is He has made clear in this, among the signs of the horizons, in the verse (p. 226) ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days?﴾ [Fussilat: 9] and what resembles it. And among the signs of the selves, in the verses ﴿Say: I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿAd and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat: 13], and those after them, and similar, and the verses ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾ [Fussilat: 49] to the end, which indicate that the human being's affair is built upon ignorance and incapacity, so that most of what he imagines is not as he imagines it. So he must reflect upon the Book of his Lord and ponder it. And Allah knows best.

Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': Reasoning from acts to their doer is clear and an evident path. Acts are of two kinds: one is the horizons, which is the totality of the world, and the second is the souls. Whoever knows his soul knows his Lord, that is, whoever knows his spirit, that it is a substance that governs the body with the governance of management, and knows its attributes, that it subsists without the body and does not need the body for its subsistence, rather the body needs it, and that it is the locus of knowledge. Whoever knows such knowledge knows his Lord and His attributes, of His oneness, His knowledge, His power, His will, and His governance over the totality of the world. That is, His existence, exalted is He, is distinct from the existence of anything else.

Since the implication was: "We continue to make that come successively, one thing after another," He joined to it His saying: ﴿until it becomes clear to them﴾, the utmost clarity by itself without the employment of thought, ﴿that it﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is the Truth﴾, the complete one in truthfulness, to which events correspond and to which the arising circumstances and the crafts bear witness. (p. 227) So they will gather upon it and turn with all their hearts toward it. No person in the Arabian Peninsula will reject it, and no two of them will dispute about it. Then they will spread through the far and wide corners of the earth, so that by them it will prevail over all religions, and through their hands it will destroy the people of disbelief in all lands, and every tyranny will vanish. Their manifestation at this time, and the weakness of the believers after the disbelief had been the cause of their increase, will be an admonition to them and to everyone who comes after them, and it necessitates steadfastness in the places of tremor, with the knowledge that Allah has made it His custom that falsehood has a wind that flutters and then calms, and a dominion that appears and then vanishes, and an assault that roams and then departs.

Since this statement alerts that in the horizons and the selves there are visible signs which those of insight read with discernment, and which they contemplate with the eyes of inner hearts, a matter that description cannot encompass, and this drives toward stripping thoughts for contemplation and reflection, and standing upon some of the subtle secrets in that, it was as if it were said: "Have they not seen with their intellects what in that is of proofs that the Qur'an is from Allah, so that it would suffice them instead of testimony from something outside themselves?" He joined to it His saying: ﴿Is it not sufficient﴾. He emphasized it by the insertion of the preposition, and made the agent definite, so He said, emphasizing with the bi (the preposition) and making definite that He is the agent, turning the speech to the description of beneficence, as a notice of gentleness toward them by returning them to Him, rather than their committing what necessitates their punishment, destruction, and eradication: ﴿that your Lord﴾, meaning the One who has done good to you by this clear statement, inimitable to humans and jinn, as a testimony that it is from Him, ﴿that He﴾, meaning, is it not sufficient that the testimony of your Lord is that He ﴿is over all things a Witness﴾, nothing of things is hidden from Him, neither this Qur'an nor anything else. He has testified for you in it by its inimitability to all creation, with everything its verses contain and its words speak. In it is the greatest good news of the completion of the affair of the religion and its victory over the transgressors. This is because everyone finds within himself that if he wants to establish a right which the one upon whom it lies denies, for the rightful owner there are witnesses whose testimony establishes it and whose coming to him with them is such that he is at ease and is not disturbed by the denial, knowing that his right will surely appear and will disgrace its opponent and subdue him. In this there is an admonition to everyone who is upon the truth and does not find anyone to help him make it manifest, for Allah is its witness, so its affair will surely become manifest. So rely upon Allah; indeed you are upon the clear truth.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 41, verse 54:

When nothing remained after this for the obstinate to say, and no doubt at all remained for the one who strays, the place for addressing those who persisted in their stubbornness came with His words, emphasizing their claim that they were upon clarity regarding their matter:

﴿Surely they are in doubt﴾, i.e., the disbelievers are in denial, disputation, skepticism and error, far from truth, ﴿concerning the meeting﴾ — and the speech turns to attributing the description of beneficence to them, as an indication that there must be the perfection of their upbringing through resurrection, for He is the most judicious of judges — ﴿with their Lord﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favor upon them by creating and providing for them, for reckoning and recompense through reward and punishment, as is the way of every wise one regarding those under his command.

Since they were openly expressing doubt about the power to resurrect, their own belief in His power over everything, including resurrection and other things, established it for them, as they acknowledged it. So He said: ﴿Surely He﴾, i.e., this Beneficent One toward them, ﴿encompasses all things﴾, i.e., of things, in their totality and their details, their universals and particulars, their roots and branches, their unseen and their witnessed, their dominion and their sovereignty, ﴿in power and knowledge﴾, of many things and few, their universals and their particulars. Soon He will gather them upon the truth and replace their doubt with submission and their skepticism with certainty and proof. So His mercy is general for all the people of existence and specific for those upon whom faith has been bestowed, which leads to the rest of security. How, then, could one conceive in the intellect that He would leave off resurrection for the Day of Judgment, which is the axis of wisdom and the place where blessing and retribution are manifested? He knows that the last of it, which praises the Book establishing resurrection and reckoning, corresponds to its first, which details the Qur'an, pouring out both kinds of mercy — the general and the specific — upon the people of the created worlds, according to what justice and beneficence require, with glad tidings for the people of faith and warning for the people of rebellion. And Allah is the Guide, and upon Him is reliance.
